      <div style="margin-top:6pt;margin-left:69.66pt;width:456pt;">
        <div style="width:456pt; line-height:12pt;">
          <font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">FedEx Freight is expected to establish an annual cash incentive plan that will reward its executive officers based on the satisfaction of a combination of corporate financial metrics and operational goals, as established by the Human Resources and Compensation Committee. </font>
        </div>
        <div style="margin-left:20pt; margin-top:12pt; width:436pt; line-height:12pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">
          <font style="letter-spacing:-0.2pt;">LTI Program</font><font style="font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </font>
        </div>
        <div style="margin-top:8pt; width:456pt; line-height:12pt;">
          <font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">The FedEx LTI program provides a long-term cash payment opportunity to members of management, including the FedEx Freight named executive officers, based upon achievement of long-term objectives for financial and stock price performance. The primary objective of FedEx&#8217;s LTI program is to motivate management to contribute to FedEx&#8217;s future success and to build long-term stockholder value and reward them accordingly. The FY23&#8211;FY25 LTI plan is described below. </font>
        </div>
        <div style="margin-top:12pt; width:456pt; line-height:12pt;font-style:italic;">
          <font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">FY23&#8211;FY25 LTI Plan</font><font style="font-style:normal;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </font>
        </div>
        <div style="margin-top:8pt; width:456pt; line-height:12pt;">
          <font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">The FY23&#8201;&#8211;&#8201;FY25 LTI plan included three financial performance metrics: (1)&#160;adjusted EPS for the three-fiscal-year period, weighted at 50% of the total payout opportunity; (2)&#160;CapEx/Revenue for the three-fiscal-year period, weighted at 25% of the total payout opportunity; and (3)&#160;relative TSR for the three-fiscal-year period, weighted at 25% of the total payout opportunity. </font>
        </div>
        <div style="margin-top:8pt; width:456pt; line-height:12pt;">
          <font style="font-style:italic;letter-spacing:0.2pt;">EPS.</font><font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> The FedEx CHRC and FedEx Board determined that EPS was an appropriate financial metric for the FY23&#8201;&#8211;&#8201;FY25 LTI plan given that growth in EPS strongly correlates to long-term stock price appreciation. Payouts under the EPS component of the FY23&#8201;&#8211;&#8201;FY25 LTI plan were determined as follows: </font>
        </div>
        <div style=" float:left; margin-left:20pt; line-height:12pt; margin-top:6.2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:left; width:10pt;white-space:nowrap;">
          <font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">&#8226;</font>
          <br >
        </div>
        <div style=" margin-top:6.2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; line-height:12pt; text-align:left; margin-left:30pt;">
          <!--blacklining:none;-->
          <font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">No payment unless the three-year average annual adjusted EPS growth rate (&#8220;EPS growth rate&#8221;) is at least 5%; </font>
        </div>
        <div style="clear:both; padding:0pt; margin:0pt;font-size:0pt;line-height:0pt;">&#8203;</div>
        <div style=" float:left; margin-left:20pt; line-height:12pt; margin-top:6.2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:left; width:10pt;white-space:nowrap;">
          <font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">&#8226;</font>
          <br >
        </div>
        <div style=" margin-top:6.2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; line-height:12pt; text-align:left; margin-left:30pt;">
          <!--blacklining:none;-->
          <font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">Target payout if the EPS growth rate is 15.0%; </font>
        </div>
        <div style="clear:both; padding:0pt; margin:0pt;font-size:0pt;line-height:0pt;">&#8203;</div>
        <div style=" float:left; margin-left:20pt; line-height:12pt; margin-top:6.2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:left; width:10pt;white-space:nowrap;">
          <font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">&#8226;</font>
          <br >
        </div>
        <div style=" margin-top:6.2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; line-height:12pt; text-align:left; margin-left:30pt;">
          <!--blacklining:none;-->
          <font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">Above-target payout if the EPS growth rate is above 15.0%, up to an amount equal to 150% of the target payout if the EPS growth rate is 17.5%; </font>
        </div>
        <div style="clear:both; padding:0pt; margin:0pt;font-size:0pt;line-height:0pt;">&#8203;</div>
        <div style=" float:left; margin-left:20pt; line-height:12pt; margin-top:6.2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:left; width:10pt;white-space:nowrap;">
          <font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">&#8226;</font>
          <br >
        </div>
        <div style=" margin-top:6.2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; line-height:12pt; text-align:left; margin-left:30pt;">
          <!--blacklining:none;-->
          <font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">Above-target payout if the EPS growth rate is above 17.5%, up to a maximum amount (equal to 200% of the target payout) if the EPS growth rate is 20.0% or higher; and </font>
        </div>
        <div style="clear:both; padding:0pt; margin:0pt;font-size:0pt;line-height:0pt;">&#8203;</div>
        <div style=" float:left; margin-left:20pt; line-height:12pt; margin-top:6.2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:left; width:10pt;white-space:nowrap;">
          <font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">&#8226;</font>
          <br >
        </div>
        <div style=" margin-top:6.2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; line-height:12pt; text-align:left; margin-left:30pt;">
          <!--blacklining:none;-->
          <font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">Below-target payout if the EPS growth rate is below 15.0%, down to a threshold amount (equal to 25% of the target payout) if the EPS growth rate is 5%. </font>
        </div>
        <div style="clear:both; padding:0pt; margin:0pt;font-size:0pt;line-height:0pt;">&#8203;</div>
        <div style="margin-top:8pt; width:456pt; line-height:12pt;">
          <font style="font-style:italic;letter-spacing:0.2pt;">CAPEX/REVENUE.</font><font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> The second metric in the FY23&#8201;&#8211;&#8201;FY25 LTI plan, CapEx/Revenue, was chosen to incentivize management to further optimize capital deployment and efficiency over the three-fiscal-year period. The FedEx CHRC and the FedEx Board chose to use CapEx/Revenue in combination with the historical EPS metric and relative TSR because it can easily be calculated from publicly available information, is easily understood by all plan participants, and works in conjunction with EPS to improve cash flow. The threshold, target, and maximum payout objectives were established based on the forecasted level of capital expenditures for the three-fiscal-year period. Payouts under the CapEx/Revenue component of the FY23&#8201;&#8211;&#8201;FY25 LTI plan were determined as follows: </font>
        </div>
        <div style=" float:left; margin-left:20pt; line-height:12pt; margin-top:6.1pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:left; width:10pt;white-space:nowrap;">
          <font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">&#8226;</font>
          <br >
        </div>
        <div style=" margin-top:6.1pt; margin-bottom:0pt; line-height:12pt; text-align:left; margin-left:30pt;">
          <!--blacklining:none;-->
          <font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">No payout unless CapEx/Revenue is at or below 7.2%; </font>
        </div>
        <div style="clear:both; padding:0pt; margin:0pt;font-size:0pt;line-height:0pt;">&#8203;</div>
        <div style=" float:left; margin-left:20pt; line-height:12pt; margin-top:6.1pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:left; width:10pt;white-space:nowrap;">
          <font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">&#8226;</font>
          <br >
        </div>
        <div style=" margin-top:6.1pt; margin-bottom:0pt; line-height:12pt; text-align:left; margin-left:30pt;">
          <!--blacklining:none;-->
          <font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">Target payout if CapEx/Revenue is at 6.9%; </font>
        </div>
        <div style="clear:both; padding:0pt; margin:0pt;font-size:0pt;line-height:0pt;">&#8203;</div>
        <div style=" float:left; margin-left:20pt; line-height:12pt; margin-top:6.09pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:left; width:10pt;white-space:nowrap;">
          <font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">&#8226;</font>
          <br >
        </div>
        <div style=" margin-top:6.09pt; margin-bottom:0pt; line-height:12pt; text-align:left; margin-left:30pt;">
          <!--blacklining:none;-->
          <font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">Above-target payout if CapEx/Revenue is below 6.9%, up to a maximum payout (equal to 150% of the target payout) if CapEx/Revenue is at or below 6.6%; and </font>
        </div>
        <div style="clear:both; padding:0pt; margin:0pt;font-size:0pt;line-height:0pt;">&#8203;</div>
        <div style=" float:left; margin-left:20pt; line-height:12pt; margin-top:6.1pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:left; width:10pt;white-space:nowrap;">
          <font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">&#8226;</font>
          <br >
        </div>
        <div style=" margin-top:6.1pt; margin-bottom:0pt; line-height:12pt; text-align:left; margin-left:30pt;">
          <!--blacklining:none;-->
          <font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">Below-target payout if CapEx/Revenue is above 6.9%, down to a threshold amount (equal to 25% of the target payout) if CapEx/Revenue is at 7.2%. </font>
        </div>
        <div style="clear:both; padding:0pt; margin:0pt;font-size:0pt;line-height:0pt;">&#8203;</div>
        <div style="margin-top:8pt; width:456pt; line-height:12pt;">
          <font style="font-style:italic;letter-spacing:0.2pt;">RELATIVE TSR.</font><font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> The third metric in the FY23&#8201;&#8211;&#8201;FY25 LTI plan, relative TSR, was chosen to directly align executive compensation with stockholder returns. The relative TSR metric measures the total return on an investment in FedEx stock to an investor (stock price appreciation plus dividends) compared to the total return of the stock of the companies in the S&amp;P 500 Index over a three-fiscal-year period. If FedEx&#8217;s TSR over the three-fiscal-year period is negative, there will be no payout, regardless of performance against </font>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div style="margin-top:2.00000000000002pt;height:12pt;margin-left:69.66pt;width:456pt;">
        <div style="margin-top:5pt; text-align:center; width:456pt; line-height:12pt;">
          <font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">&#160;</font>
          <br >
        </div>
      </div>
      <div style="margin-top:2pt;margin-bottom:21.86pt;margin-left:69.66pt;width:456pt;">
        <div style="margin-top:5pt; text-align:center; width:456pt; line-height:12pt;">
          <font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">116</font>
          <br >
        </div>
      </div>
      <hr >
    </div>
    <div style="page-break-after:always; width:595.3pt;margin-left:auto;margin-right:auto;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;font-variant:normal;text-transform:none;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;font-size:10pt;">
      <div style="padding:0pt;margin:0pt;font-family:calibri, arial, sans-serif;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;font-size:8pt;line-height:8pt;">
        <a style="text-decoration:none;color:#003366;" href="#TOC">TABLE OF CONTENTS</a>
      </div>
      <div style="margin-top:15.85pt;height:24pt;margin-left:69.66pt;width:456pt;">
        <div style="margin-top:17pt; width:456pt; line-height:12pt;">
          <font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">&#160;</font>
          <br >
        </div>
      </div>
      <div style="margin-top:6pt;margin-left:69.66pt;width:456pt;">
        <div style="width:456pt; line-height:11.5pt;">
          <font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">the companies in the S&amp;P 500 Index. Payouts under the relative TSR component of the FY23&#8201;&#8211;&#8201;FY25 LTI plan were determined as follows: </font>
        </div>
        <div style=" float:left; margin-left:20pt; line-height:12pt; margin-top:5.8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:left; width:10pt;white-space:nowrap;">
          <font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">&#8226;</font>
          <br >
        </div>
        <div style=" margin-top:5.8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; line-height:12pt; text-align:left; margin-left:30pt;">
          <!--blacklining:none;-->
          <font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">No payout unless relative TSR is above the 25th&#160;percentile; </font>
        </div>
        <div style="clear:both; padding:0pt; margin:0pt;font-size:0pt;line-height:0pt;">&#8203;</div>
        <div style=" float:left; margin-left:20pt; line-height:12pt; margin-top:5.8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:left; width:10pt;white-space:nowrap;">
          <font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">&#8226;</font>
          <br >
        </div>
        <div style=" margin-top:5.8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; line-height:12pt; text-align:left; margin-left:30pt;">
          <!--blacklining:none;-->
          <font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">Target payout if relative TSR is above the 50th&#160;percentile, up to the 75th&#160;percentile; </font>
        </div>
        <div style="clear:both; padding:0pt; margin:0pt;font-size:0pt;line-height:0pt;">&#8203;</div>
        <div style=" float:left; margin-left:20pt; line-height:12pt; margin-top:5.8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:left; width:10pt;white-space:nowrap;">
          <font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">&#8226;</font>
          <br >
        </div>
        <div style=" margin-top:5.8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; line-height:12pt; text-align:left; margin-left:30pt;">
          <!--blacklining:none;-->
          <font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">Maximum payout (equal to 200% of the target payout) if relative TSR is above the 75th&#160;percentile; and </font>
        </div>
        <div style="clear:both; padding:0pt; margin:0pt;font-size:0pt;line-height:0pt;">&#8203;</div>
        <div style=" float:left; margin-left:20pt; line-height:12pt; margin-top:5.8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:left; width:10pt;white-space:nowrap;">
          <font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">&#8226;</font>
          <br >
        </div>
        <div style=" margin-top:5.8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; line-height:12pt; text-align:left; margin-left:30pt;">
          <!--blacklining:none;-->
          <font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">50% of the target payout if relative TSR is at the 50th&#160;percentile or below, down to the 26th&#160;percentile. </font>
        </div>
        <div style="clear:both; padding:0pt; margin:0pt;font-size:0pt;line-height:0pt;">&#8203;</div>
        <div style="margin-top:12pt; width:456pt; line-height:12pt;font-style:italic;">
          <font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">Mark-to-Market Retirement Plans Accounting and Other Adjustments to EPS for LTI Plan&#160;Purposes</font><font style="font-style:normal;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </font>
        </div>
        <div style="margin-top:8pt; width:456pt; line-height:11.5pt;">
          <font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">The FY23&#8201;&#8211;&#8201;FY25 LTI plan, as well as all active LTI plans, include the achievement of FedEx EPS goals for the three-fiscal-year period as the most heavily weighted performance metric. The LTI plan design provides for payouts for the EPS plan component that correspond to specific EPS goals established by the FedEx Board that represent total growth in EPS (over a base year) for the three-year term of the LTI plan. </font>
        </div>
        <div style="margin-top:8pt; width:456pt; line-height:11.5pt;">
          <font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">The mark-to-market retirement plans accounting adjustments (&#8220;MTM Adjustments&#8221;), which reflect year-end and other adjustments to the valuation of FedEx&#8217;s defined benefit pension and other postretirement plans, can vary dramatically from year-to-year, as they are significantly impacted by changes in interest rates and the financial markets. As a result, the FedEx Board, upon the recommendation of the FedEx CHRC, previously determined that MTM Adjustments will be excluded from EPS calculations under all FedEx LTI plans. In addition, the FedEx Board, upon the recommendation of the FedEx CHRC, approved the exclusion of business optimization costs from fiscal 2023, 2024, 2025, and 2026 EPS for purposes of the FY23&#8201;&#8211;&#8201;FY25 LTI plan and all active LTI plans. The FedEx Board determined that, by excluding these costs, payouts, if any, under the LTI plans will more accurately reflect FedEx&#8217;s core financial performance. </font>
        </div>
        <div style="margin-top:8pt; width:456pt; line-height:11.5pt;">
          <font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">The FedEx Board, upon the recommendation of the FedEx CHRC, approved the exclusion of certain other items from fiscal 2022, 2023, 2024, and 2025 EPS for purposes of FedEx&#8217;s FY23&#8201;&#8211;&#8201;FY25, FY24&#8201;&#8211;&#8201;FY26, and FY25&#8201;&#8211;&#8201;FY27 LTI plans, and for establishing the baseline EPS for the FY23&#8201;&#8211;&#8201;FY25 LTI plan and all active LTI plans. The FedEx Board determined that, by excluding each of these items, payouts, if any, under the LTI plans will more accurately reflect FedEx&#8217;s core financial performance in these&#160;years, as applicable. A discussion of the items excluded for each fiscal year and full reconciliations showing the individual adjustments to the GAAP EPS measure for the applicable fiscal year, as compared to the non-GAAP EPS measure used for each applicable LTI plan, please refer to Appendix&#160;C to the FedEx proxy statement filed in respect of the fiscal year ended May&#160;31, 2025. </font>
        </div>
        <div style="margin-top:8pt; width:456pt; line-height:11.5pt;">
          <font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">During fiscal 2023, FedEx repurchased 9,180,752 shares under its stock repurchase program. Because the positive impact on EPS resulting from these stock repurchases did not reflect core business performance, the FedEx Board, upon the recommendation of the FedEx CHRC, approved the exclusion of the impact of the fiscal 2023 stock repurchases in excess of that which offset dilution from equity awards from EPS for fiscal 2023 for the purpose of calculating attainment under the FY23&#8201;&#8211;&#8201;FY25 LTI plan. Beginning in fiscal 2024, the impact of stock repurchases in excess of that which offset dilution from equity awards was not excluded from EPS for LTI plan purposes. </font>
        </div>
        <div style="margin-top:12pt; width:456pt; line-height:12pt;font-style:italic;">
          <font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">Fiscal 2025 LTI Performance and Payouts</font><font style="font-style:normal;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </font>
        </div>
        <div style="margin-top:8pt; width:456pt; line-height:11.5pt;">
          <font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">For the FY23&#8201;&#8211;&#8201;FY25 LTI plan, the baseline EPS over which the three-fiscal-year average annual EPS growth rate goals are measured was $20.61. For purposes of establishing the baseline EPS for the FY23&#8201;&#8211;&#8201;FY25 LTI plan, fiscal 2022 GAAP EPS of $14.33 was adjusted to exclude (i)&#160;MTM Adjustments ($4.49 per diluted share), (ii)&#160;fiscal 2022 business realignment costs ($0.80 per diluted share), (iii)&#160;costs related to a legacy FedEx Ground legal matter incurred in fiscal 2022 ($0.60 per diluted share), and fiscal 2022 TNT Express integration expenses ($0.39 per diluted share). </font>
        </div>
        <div style="margin-top:8pt; width:456pt; line-height:11.5pt;">
          <font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">The following table presents the EPS, CapEx/Revenue, and relative TSR threshold (minimum), target, and maximum objectives under FedEx&#8217;s FY23&#8201;&#8211;&#8201;FY25 LTI plan, which was established by the FedEx Board in June&#160;2022, and FedEx&#8217;s actual adjusted EPS, CapEx/Revenue, and relative TSR under the plan for the three-fiscal-year period ended May&#160;31, 2025: </font>
        </div>

        <div style="margin-top:7.9pt; width:456pt; line-height:11.5pt;">
          <font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">FedEx Freight is expected to establish a long-term equity-based incentive plan that will reward its executive officers based on the satisfaction of long-term corporate financial metrics, as established by the Human Resources and Compensation Committee. </font>
        </div>
        <div style="margin-left:20pt; margin-top:12pt; width:436pt; line-height:12pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">
          <font style="letter-spacing:-0.2pt;">Promotional Bonuses</font><font style="font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </font>
        </div>
        <div style="margin-top:8pt; width:456pt; line-height:11.5pt;">
          <font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">FedEx provides promotional bonuses to senior officers, which are generally paid in two installments over one year upon an officer&#8217;s promotion. In August&#160;2024, Mr.&#160;Lyons received the first installment ($25,000) of a promotional bonus of $50,000 related to his appointment as Senior Vice President, FedEx Custom Critical and Freight Strategy at FedEx Freight. </font>
        </div>
        <div style="margin-left:20pt; margin-top:12pt; width:436pt; line-height:12pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">
          <font style="letter-spacing:-0.2pt;">Long-Term Equity Incentives&#8201;&#8212;&#8201;Stock Options and Restricted Stock</font><font style="font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </font>
        </div>
        <div style="margin-top:8pt; width:456pt; line-height:11.5pt;">
          <font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">FedEx&#8217;s primary objective in providing long-term equity incentives to its officers is to further align their interests with those of FedEx&#8217;s stockholders by facilitating significant ownership of FedEx stock by the officers. This creates a direct link between their compensation and long-term stockholder return. Equity awards also serve as an effective retention and motivational vehicle, focusing officers on the long-term success of FedEx and rewarding them when the stock price appreciates. During fiscal 2025 the FedEx CHRC again reviewed FedEx&#8217;s long-term equity incentive programs and determined that they continue to be appropriate for FedEx. </font>
        </div>
        <div style="margin-top:12pt; width:456pt; line-height:12pt;font-style:italic;">
          <font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">Amount</font><font style="font-style:normal;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </font>
        </div>
        <div style="margin-top:8pt; width:456pt; line-height:12pt;">
          <font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">Stock options and restricted stock are generally granted to senior officers on an annual basis. As discussed above, an officer&#8217;s position and level of responsibility are the primary factors that determine the number of options and shares of restricted stock awarded to the officer in the annual grant. The number of stock options and restricted shares awarded at each management level can vary from year to year. In determining how many options and shares of restricted stock should be awarded at each level, the following factors may be considered: </font>
        </div>
        <div style=" float:left; margin-left:20pt; line-height:12pt; margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:left; width:10pt;white-space:nowrap;">
          <font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">&#8226;</font>
          <br >
        </div>
        <div style=" margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; line-height:12pt; text-align:left; margin-left:30pt;">
          <!--blacklining:none;-->
          <font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">Target total direct compensation (&#8220;TDC&#8221;) levels and referenced survey data&#8201;&#8212;&#8201;as discussed above, FedEx includes the total target value of all annual equity-based awards (including tax payments for restricted stock awards) in its calculation of target TDC levels for FedEx&#8217;s officers; </font>
        </div>
        <div style="clear:both; padding:0pt; margin:0pt;font-size:0pt;line-height:0pt;">&#8203;</div>
      </div>
      <div style="margin-top:2.00000000000002pt;height:12pt;margin-left:69.66pt;width:456pt;">
        <div style="margin-top:5pt; text-align:center; width:456pt; line-height:12pt;">
          <font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">&#160;</font>
          <br >
        </div>
      </div>
      <div style="margin-top:2pt;margin-bottom:21.86pt;margin-left:69.66pt;width:456pt;">
        <div style="margin-top:5pt; text-align:center; width:456pt; line-height:12pt;">
          <font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">118</font>
          <br >
        </div>
      </div>
      <hr >
    </div>
    <div style="page-break-after:always; width:595.3pt;margin-left:auto;margin-right:auto;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;font-variant:normal;text-transform:none;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;font-size:10pt;">
      <div style="padding:0pt;margin:0pt;font-family:calibri, arial, sans-serif;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;font-size:8pt;line-height:8pt;">
        <a style="text-decoration:none;color:#003366;" href="#TOC">TABLE OF CONTENTS</a>
      </div>
      <div style="margin-top:15.85pt;height:24pt;margin-left:69.66pt;width:456pt;">
        <div style="margin-top:17pt; width:456pt; line-height:12pt;">
          <font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">&#160;</font>
          <br >
        </div>
      </div>
      <div style="margin-top:6pt;margin-left:69.66pt;width:456pt;">
        <div style=" float:left; margin-left:20pt; line-height:12pt; text-align:left; width:10pt;white-space:nowrap;">
          <font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">&#8226;</font>
          <br >
        </div>
        <div style=" line-height:12pt; text-align:left; margin-left:30pt;">
          <!--blacklining:none;-->
          <font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">The total number of shares then available to be granted; and </font>
        </div>
        <div style="clear:both; padding:0pt; margin:0pt;font-size:0pt;line-height:0pt;">&#8203;</div>
        <div style=" float:left; margin-left:20pt; line-height:12pt; margin-top:6.99pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:left; width:10pt;white-space:nowrap;">
          <font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">&#8226;</font>
          <br >
        </div>
        <div style=" margin-top:6.99pt; margin-bottom:0pt; line-height:12pt; text-align:left; margin-left:30pt;">
          <!--blacklining:none;-->
          <font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">Potential stockholder dilution. </font>
        </div>
        <div style="clear:both; padding:0pt; margin:0pt;font-size:0pt;line-height:0pt;">&#8203;</div>
        <div style="margin-top:8pt; width:456pt; line-height:12pt;">
          <font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">Other factors that may be considered, especially with respect to special grants outside of the annual-grant framework, include the promotion of an officer or the desire to retain a valued officer or recognize a particular officer&#8217;s contributions. None of these factors is given any particular weight and the specific factors used may vary among individual officers. </font>
        </div>
        <div style="margin-top:12pt; width:456pt; line-height:12pt;font-style:italic;">
          <font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">Timing</font><font style="font-style:normal;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </font>
        </div>
        <div style="margin-top:8pt; width:456pt; line-height:12pt;">
          <font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">Stock option and restricted stock awards are generally made to officers on an annual basis according to a pre-established schedule. The FedEx CHRC approves the grant of all equity awards to FedEx&#8217;s Section&#160;16 officers (such as Mr.&#160;Smith) and all non-management FedEx Board members, and may, to the extent permitted by FedEx&#8217;s equity compensation plans, delegate to one or more FedEx officers the authority to grant equity awards to other eligible individuals (such as the other FedEx Freight named executive officers). </font>
        </div>
        <div style="margin-top:8pt; width:456pt; line-height:12pt;">
          <font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">Throughout the year, equity awards are made to new hires, promoted employees, and, in certain circumstances, as a reward for exceptional performance or for motivational or retention purposes. When the FedEx CHRC approves a special grant outside of the annual-grant framework, such grants are typically made at a regularly scheduled meeting and the grant date of the awards is the approval date or the next business day, if the meeting does not fall on a business day. If the grant is made in connection with the promotion of an individual or the election of an officer, the grant date may be the effective date of the individual&#8217;s promotion or the officer&#8217;s election, if such effective date is after the approval date. If the meeting date falls within a blackout period when trading in FedEx securities is prohibited under the FedEx Securities Manual, the FedEx CHRC may approve the awards but make them effective as of a future grant date that falls outside of such blackout period. </font>
        </div>
        <div style="margin-top:8pt; width:456pt; line-height:12pt;">
          <font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">In addition, with respect to the timing of FedEx&#8217;s equity awards: </font>
        </div>
        <div style=" float:left; margin-left:20pt; line-height:12pt; margin-top:6.79pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:left; width:10pt;white-space:nowrap;">
          <font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">&#8226;</font>
          <br >
        </div>
        <div style=" margin-top:6.79pt; margin-bottom:0pt; line-height:12pt; text-align:left; margin-left:30pt;">
          <!--blacklining:none;-->
          <font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">FedEx does not time equity-based awards in coordination with the release of material, non-public information and has never had a practice of doing so; and </font>
        </div>
        <div style="clear:both; padding:0pt; margin:0pt;font-size:0pt;line-height:0pt;">&#8203;</div>
        <div style=" float:left; margin-left:20pt; line-height:12pt; margin-top:7pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:left; width:10pt;white-space:nowrap;">
          <font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">&#8226;</font>
          <br >
        </div>
        <div style=" margin-top:7pt; margin-bottom:0pt; line-height:12pt; text-align:left; margin-left:30pt;">
          <!--blacklining:none;-->
          <font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">FedEx has never timed and does not plan to time the release of material, non-public information for the purpose of affecting the value of employee or FedEx Board compensation. </font>
        </div>
        <div style="clear:both; padding:0pt; margin:0pt;font-size:0pt;line-height:0pt;">&#8203;</div>
        <div style="margin-top:12pt; width:456pt; line-height:12pt;font-style:italic;">
          <font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">Pricing</font><font style="font-style:normal;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </font>
        </div>
        <div style="margin-top:8pt; width:456pt; line-height:12pt;">
          <font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">The exercise price of stock options granted under FedEx&#8217;s equity incentive plans is equal to the fair market value of FedEx&#8217;s common stock on the date of grant. Under the terms of FedEx&#8217;s equity incentive plans, the fair market value on the grant date is defined as the average of the high and low trading prices of FedEx&#8217;s common stock on the Exchange on that day. FedEx believes this is the most equitable method for determining the exercise price of FedEx&#8217;s stock option awards given the intra-day price volatility often shown by FedEx&#8217;s stock. </font>
        </div>
        <div style="margin-top:12pt; width:456pt; line-height:12pt;font-style:italic;">
          <font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">Vesting</font><font style="font-style:normal;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </font>
        </div>
        <div style="margin-top:8pt; width:456pt; line-height:12pt;">
          <font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">Stock options and restricted stock granted to senior officers generally vest ratably over four&#160;years beginning on the first anniversary of the grant date. This four-year vesting period is intended to further encourage the retention of FedEx&#8217;s officers, since unvested stock options are forfeited upon termination of the officer&#8217;s employment for any reason other than death or permanent disability and unvested restricted stock is forfeited upon termination of the officer&#8217;s employment for any reason other than death, permanent disability, or retirement. </font>
        </div>
        <div style="margin-top:8pt; width:456pt; line-height:12pt;">
          <font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">FedEx Freight is expected to implement a long-term equity incentive program for its executive officers that aligns their interests with those of its stockholders by facilitating significant ownership of FedEx Freight stock by the officers. It is expected that each of FedEx Freight&#8217;s executive officers will participate in the long-term equity incentive program. </font>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div style="margin-top:2.00000000000002pt;height:12pt;margin-left:69.66pt;width:456pt;">
        <div style="margin-top:5pt; text-align:center; width:456pt; line-height:12pt;">
          <font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">&#160;</font>
          <br >
        </div>
      </div>
      <div style="margin-top:2pt;margin-bottom:21.86pt;margin-left:69.66pt;width:456pt;">
        <div style="margin-top:5pt; text-align:center; width:456pt; line-height:12pt;">
          <font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">119</font>
          <br >
        </div>

Also includes a one-time special grant of 388 shares of restricted stock and 225 stock options awarded to Mr.&#160;Lyons on September&#160;23, 2024 in connection with his promotion to Senior Vice President, FedEx Custom Critical and Freight Strategy at FedEx Freight. </font>

        <div style="margin-top:12pt; width:456pt; line-height:12pt;font-style:italic;">
          <font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">Treatment of Long-Term Equity Incentive Compensation in Connection with the Spin-Off</font><font style="font-style:normal;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </font>

          <font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">FedEx long-term equity compensation awards will be treated as described in the section entitled &#8220;The Spin-Off&#8201;&#8212;&#8201;Treatment of Equity Awards.&#8221; </font>
        </div>
        <div style="margin-top:12pt; width:456pt; line-height:12pt;font-style:italic;">
          <font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">FedEx Freight 2026 Omnibus Stock Incentive Plan</font><font style="font-style:normal;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </font>
        </div>
        <div style="margin-top:8pt; width:456pt; line-height:11.5pt;">
          <font style="font-style:italic;letter-spacing:0.2pt;">Introduction.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</font><font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">Prior to the closing of the Spin-Off, we intend to adopt the FedEx Freight 2026 Omnibus Stock Incentive Plan (the &#8220;2026 Plan&#8221;), subject to approval by FedEx in its capacity as our sole stockholder. The 2026 Plan is expected to become effective on the Distribution Date. No awards may be granted under the 2026 Plan prior to the closing of the Spin-Off. This summary of the 2026 Plan is subject to and qualified in its entirety by reference to the full text of the 2026 Plan, the form of which is filed as an exhibit to our Registration Statement on Form 10 to which this Information Statement is a part. </font>
        </div>
        <div style="margin-top:8pt; width:456pt; line-height:11.5pt;">
          <font style="font-style:italic;letter-spacing:0.2pt;">Purpose of the 2026 Plan.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</font><font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">The purpose of the 2026 Plan is to aid the Company in retaining, attracting, and rewarding non-employee directors and designated employees and service providers of outstanding ability and to motivate them to exert their best efforts to achieve the Company&#8217;s long-term goals. The Board believes that increased ownership of our common stock by directors, employees, and service providers, and compensation that is otherwise linked to the value of our common stock, will further align their interests with those of the Company&#8217;s other stockholders and will promote the Company&#8217;s long-term success and the creation of long-term stockholder value. </font>
        </div>
        <div style="margin-top:8pt; width:456pt; line-height:11.5pt;">
          <font style="font-style:italic;letter-spacing:0.2pt;">Administration of the 2026 Plan.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</font><font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">The 2026 Plan will be administered by our Human Resources and Compensation Committee (or such successor committee or subcommittee of our Board that is designated by our Board to administer the 2026 Plan consisting of not less than two members who qualify as &#8220;independent directors&#8221; under Section&#160;303A of the New York Stock Exchange Listed Company Manual and are &#8220;non-employee directors&#8221; as defined in Rule&#160;16b-3 under the Exchange Act). </font>
        </div>
        <div style="margin-top:8pt; width:456pt; line-height:11.5pt;">
          <font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">Subject to the express provisions of the 2026 Plan, our Human Resources and Compensation Committee will have full and exclusive power, authority, and discretion to take any and all actions necessary, appropriate, or advisable for the administration of the 2026 Plan, including the following: </font>
        </div>

Any shares related to awards that are settled in cash or other consideration in lieu of shares and any shares that are withheld or deducted from an award or delivered by a participant to satisfy tax withholding requirements relating to full-value awards (i.e., awards other than stock options or stock appreciation rights) will be available again for issuance pursuant to awards granted under the 2026 Plan. However, shares will not be added back to the share reserve and made available for issuance pursuant to awards granted under the 2026 Plan if (i)&#160;the shares are withheld or deducted from an award or delivered by a participant to satisfy tax withholding requirements relating to stock options or stock appreciation rights, (ii)&#160;the shares are used for payment of the exercise price of a stock option, or (iii)&#160;the shares are repurchased on the open market with proceeds of a stock option exercise. In addition, to the extent that the full number of shares subject to a stock option or share-settled stock appreciation right is not issued upon exercise for any reason, including by reason of a net settlement or net exercise, then all shares that were covered by the exercised stock option or stock appreciation right will not be available for issuance pursuant to awards granted under the 2026 Plan. </font>

          <font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">FedEx Freight Employee Stock Purchase Plan</font><font style="font-style:normal;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </font>

        <div style="margin-top:8pt; width:456pt; line-height:12pt;">
          <font style="font-style:italic;letter-spacing:0.2pt;">Introduction.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</font><font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">Prior to the closing of the Spin-Off, we intend to adopt the FedEx Freight Employee Stock Purchase Plan (the &#8220;ESPP&#8221;), subject to approval by FedEx in its capacity as our sole stockholder. The ESPP is expected to become effective as of the Distribution Date. No awards may be granted under the ESPP prior to the closing of the Spin-Off, and the Board has not authorized an initial offering period under the ESPP. This summary of the ESPP is subject to and qualified in its entirety by reference to the full text of the ESPP, the form of which is filed as an exhibit to our Registration Statement on Form 10 to which this Information Statement is a part. </font>
        </div>
        <div style="margin-top:8pt; width:456pt; line-height:12pt;">
          <font style="font-style:italic;letter-spacing:0.2pt;">Purpose of the ESPP</font><font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The purpose of the ESPP is to facilitate and encourage our employees&#8217; participation in the ownership and economic progress of our company by providing our employees with an opportunity to purchase shares of our common stock and to receive additional shares of our common stock linked to their purchases. The ESPP is not intended to qualify as an &#8220;employee stock purchase plan&#8221; under Section&#160;423 of the Code. </font>
        </div>
        <div style="margin-top:8pt; width:456pt; line-height:12pt;">
          <font style="font-style:italic;letter-spacing:0.2pt;">Summary of Expected Plan&#160;Terms.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</font><font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">A total of&#8199;&#8199;&#8199;&#8199;&#8199;&#8199;&#8199;shares of our common stock will be reserved and available for issuance under the ESPP. The maximum number of shares of our common stock reserved for issuance under the ESPP will be subject to an annual increase on the first day of each fiscal year during the term of the ESPP, beginning on and including January&#160;1, 2027, and ending on and including January&#160;1, 2035, equal to the lesser of (x)&#8199;&#8199;&#8199;&#8199;&#8199;&#8199;&#8199;% of the aggregate number of fully diluted shares of our common stock issued and outstanding on December&#160;31 of the immediately preceding fiscal year and (y)&#160;such smaller number of shares of our common stock as is determined by our Human Resources and Compensation Committee, which will administer the ESPP. </font>
        </div>
        <div style="margin-top:8pt; width:456pt; line-height:12pt;">
          <font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">Our Human Resources and Compensation Committee will have full and exclusive authority to construe, interpret, and apply the terms of the ESPP, determine eligibility to participate under the ESPP, and adjudicate and resolve disputes under the ESPP. </font>

        <div style="width:456pt; line-height:11.5pt;">
          <font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">Our full-time employees and the full-time employees of our subsidiaries who are employed on the first day of any offering period may participate in the ESPP. In order to participate in the ESPP, an employee who is eligible at the beginning of an offering period will authorize payroll deductions on an after-tax basis for each pay date during the offering period. A participant may not make any separate cash payment into his or her account unless specifically provided for in the offering, but may alter the amount of his or her payroll deductions during an offering period and may withdraw from participation. No participant may accrue options to purchase shares of our common stock in excess of the applicable annual limit determined by our Human Resources and Compensation Committee. </font>
        </div>
        <div style="margin-top:8pt; width:456pt; line-height:11.5pt;">
          <font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">One or more offering periods may be established under the ESPP in the discretion of our Human Resources and Compensation Committee. Each offering will commence at such time and be of such duration as determined by our Human Resources and Compensation Committee prior to the start of the applicable offering period, with purchases being made on the last trading day of each offering period. On the last day of an offering period, also referred to as the exercise date, a participant&#8217;s option to purchase shares of our common stock will be exercised, and the participant&#8217;s accumulated payroll deductions will be used to purchase the maximum number of full shares of our common stock subject to such option. Unless determined otherwise by our Human Resources and Compensation Committee in advance of an offering, the purchase price of shares of our common stock under the ESPP will be equal to the fair market value of a share of our common stock on the exercise date of an option. Participants are not entitled to any dividends or voting rights with respect to options to purchase shares of our common stock under the ESPP. Shares received upon exercise of an option will be entitled to receive dividends on the same basis as other outstanding shares of our common stock. </font>
        </div>
        <div style="margin-top:8pt; width:456pt; line-height:11.5pt;">
          <font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">Each participant that receives purchased shares will also receive a conditional right to receive additional shares of our common stock under the ESPP linked to such purchased shares, which we refer to as a matching award. Matching awards will be granted automatically on the same day as the exercise date for the related purchased shares. The number of shares of our common stock subject to a matching award will be equal to the number of purchased shares to which it is linked. Matching awards generally will be released on the first anniversary of the applicable grant date, subject to the participant&#8217;s continued employment with us or our subsidiaries through that date. The number of shares of our common stock subject to a matching award that are released will be equal to the number of related purchased shares that the participant holds in the participant&#8217;s ESPP brokerage account as of the release date. Matching awards will lapse to the extent the related purchased shares are transferred or sold before the applicable release date. Our Human Resources and Compensation Committee may choose to settle any matching award partly or fully in cash, and matching awards may include dividend equivalents. </font>
        </div>
        <div style="margin-top:8pt; width:456pt; line-height:11.5pt;">
          <font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">If a matching award lapses for any reason (in whole or in part), any unissued or forfeited shares of our common stock subject to the matching award will be added back to the ESPP share reserve and available again for issuance under the ESPP. Any shares of our common stock related to a matching award that is settled in cash in lieu of shares will be added back to the ESPP share reserve and available again for issuance under the ESPP. Shares withheld or deducted by the Company to satisfy tax withholding requirements relating to matching awards will be added back to the ESPP share reserve and available again for issuance under the ESPP. </font>
        </div>
        <div style="margin-top:8pt; width:456pt; line-height:11.5pt;">
          <font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">A participant may withdraw all, but not less than all, of the payroll deductions credited to the participant&#8217;s account for the applicable offering period by delivery of notice prior to the exercise date for such offering period. If a participant&#8217;s employment is terminated on or before the exercise date, the participant will be deemed to have elected to withdraw from the ESPP, and the accumulated payroll deductions held in the participant&#8217;s account will be returned to the participant or the participant&#8217;s beneficiary (in the event of the participant&#8217;s death). Any unreleased matching awards held by the participant on the termination date will automatically lapse; however, if a participant&#8217;s employment with us or our subsidiaries terminates due to their death or disability prior to the release date of any matching awards, the maximum number of shares of our common stock subject to the matching award will be released as of the termination date. </font>
        </div>
        <div style="margin-top:8pt; width:456pt; line-height:11.5pt;">
          <font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">In the event of a dividend or distribution, stock split, reverse stock split, spin-off, or other similar transaction, or other change in corporate structure affecting shares of our common stock or their value, the number of shares of common stock reserved for issuance under the ESPP, the purchase price per share, the maximum number of shares of common stock that may be purchased on an exercise date, and the number and kind </font>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div style="margin-top:2.00000000000002pt;height:12pt;margin-left:69.66pt;width:456pt;">
        <div style="margin-top:5pt; text-align:center; width:456pt; line-height:12pt;">
          <font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">&#160;</font>
          <br >
        </div>

          <font style="font-weight:bold;letter-spacing:-0.2pt;">Use of corporate aircraft by Mr.&#160;Smith to attend meetings of outside companies:</font><font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> FedEx maintains a fleet of corporate aircraft that is used primarily for business travel by FedEx employees. FedEx has a written policy that sets forth guidelines and procedures regarding personal use of FedEx corporate aircraft. The policy requires officers to pay FedEx two times the cost of fuel for personal trips, plus applicable passenger ticket taxes and fees. These payments are intended to approximate the incremental cost to FedEx of personal corporate aircraft usage. </font>
        </div>
        <div style="clear:both; padding:0pt; margin:0pt;font-size:0pt;line-height:0pt;">&#8203;</div>

          <!--blacklining:none;-->
          <font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">Compensation is included in the table above for corporate aircraft travel by Mr.&#160;Smith to attend board or stockholder meetings of outside companies or organizations for which he served as a director to the extent that the aggregate incremental cost to FedEx of all such travel exceeded the amount FedEx was reimbursed for such travel. The incremental cost to FedEx of personal use of corporate aircraft is calculated based on the variable operating cost to FedEx, which includes the cost of fuel, aircraft maintenance, crew travel, landing fees, ramp fees, and other smaller variable costs. Because FedEx corporate aircraft are used primarily for business travel, fixed costs that do not change based on usage, such as pilots&#8217; salaries and purchase and lease costs, are excluded from this calculation. </font>

FedEx reimburses officers for taxes relating to imputed income for business-related travel. </font>

To the extent the services and equipment are provided by third parties (e.g., out-of-town transportation and other security-related expenses and home security system installation, maintenance, and monitoring), we have included in the table above for Mr.&#160;Smith the amounts paid by FedEx for such services and equipment. To the extent the security services are provided by FedEx employees, we have included for Mr.&#160;Smith amounts representing: (a)&#160;the number of hours of service provided by each such employee multiplied by (b)&#160;the total hourly compensation cost of the employee (including, among other things, pension and other benefit costs). </font>

    <div style="page-break-after:always; width:595.3pt;margin-left:auto;margin-right:auto;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;font-variant:normal;text-transform:none;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;font-size:10pt;">
      <div style="padding:0pt;margin:0pt;font-family:calibri, arial, sans-serif;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;font-size:8pt;line-height:8pt;">
        <a style="text-decoration:none;color:#003366;" href="#TOC">TABLE OF CONTENTS</a>
      </div>
      <div style="margin-top:15.85pt;height:24pt;margin-left:69.66pt;width:456pt;">
        <div style="margin-top:17pt; width:456pt; line-height:12pt;">
          <font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">&#160;</font>
          <br >
        </div>
      </div>
      <div style="margin-top:6pt;margin-left:69.66pt;width:456pt;">
        <div style="width:456pt;">
          <div style="margin-left: 0pt; width: 108pt; margin-top: 0pt; font-size: 1pt; line-height: 0pt; border-bottom: 1pt solid #000000; ">&#8203;</div>
        </div>
        <div style=" float:left; margin-top:10.79pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:left; width:20pt;white-space:nowrap;">
          <font style=" position:relative; bottom:4.25pt;font-size:7.5pt;letter-spacing:0.15pt;">(1)</font>
          <br >
        </div>
        <div style=" margin-top:9.79pt; margin-bottom:0pt; line-height:12pt; text-align:left; margin-left:20pt;">
          <!--blacklining:none;-->
          <font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">The exercise price of the options is the fair market value of FedEx common stock (the average of the high and low prices of the stock on the Exchange) on the grant date. </font>
        </div>
        <div style="clear:both; padding:0pt; margin:0pt;font-size:0pt;line-height:0pt;">&#8203;</div>
        <div style=" float:left; line-height:12pt; margin-top:5.79pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:left; width:20pt;white-space:nowrap;">
          <font style=" position:relative; bottom:4.25pt;font-size:7.5pt;letter-spacing:0.15pt;">(2)</font>
          <br >
        </div>
        <div style=" margin-top:5.79pt; margin-bottom:0pt; line-height:12pt; text-align:left; margin-left:20pt;">
          <!--blacklining:none;-->
          <font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">Represents the grant date fair value of each equity-based award, computed in accordance with FASB ASC Topic 718. See note 3 to the Summary Compensation Table for information regarding the assumptions used in the calculation of these amounts. </font>
        </div>
        <div style="clear:both; padding:0pt; margin:0pt;font-size:0pt;line-height:0pt;">&#8203;</div>
        <div style=" float:left; line-height:12pt; margin-top:5.89pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:left; width:20pt;white-space:nowrap;">
          <font style=" position:relative; bottom:4.25pt;font-size:7.5pt;letter-spacing:0.15pt;">(3)</font>
          <br >
        </div>
        <div style=" margin-top:5.89pt; margin-bottom:0pt; line-height:12pt; text-align:left; margin-left:20pt;">
          <!--blacklining:none;-->
          <font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">Shares of restricted FedEx stock awarded to the FedEx Freight named executive officers generally vest ratably over four&#160;years beginning on the first anniversary of the grant date. Holders of restricted stock are entitled to vote such shares and receive any dividends paid on FedEx common stock. FedEx pays the taxes resulting from a restricted stock award on behalf of the recipient (these tax payments are included in the &#8220;All Other Compensation&#8221; column in the Summary Compensation Table). See &#8220;&#8212;&#160;Compensation Elements and Fiscal 2025 Amounts&#8201;&#8212;&#8201;Long-Term Equity Incentives&#8201;&#8212;&#8201;Stock Options and Restricted Stock&#8221; for further discussion of restricted stock awards and &#8220;The Spin-Off&#8201;&#8212;&#8201;Treatment of Equity Awards&#8221; above for discussion of the treatment of shares of restricted FedEx stock held by FedEx Freight employees in connection with the Spin-Off. </font>
        </div>
        <div style="clear:both; padding:0pt; margin:0pt;font-size:0pt;line-height:0pt;">&#8203;</div>
        <div style=" float:left; line-height:12pt; margin-top:5.89pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:left; width:20pt;white-space:nowrap;">
          <font style=" position:relative; bottom:4.25pt;font-size:7.5pt;letter-spacing:0.15pt;">(4)</font>
          <br >
        </div>
        <div style=" margin-top:5.89pt; margin-bottom:0pt; line-height:12pt; text-align:left; margin-left:20pt;">
          <!--blacklining:none;-->
          <font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">Stock options granted to the FedEx Freight named executive officers generally vest ratably over four&#160;years beginning on the first anniversary of the grant date. The options may not be transferred in any manner other than by will or the laws of descent and distribution and may be exercised during the lifetime of the optionee only by the optionee. See &#8220;&#8212; Compensation Elements and Fiscal 2025 Amounts&#8201;&#8212;&#8201;Long-Term Equity Incentives&#8201;&#8212;&#8201;Stock Options and Restricted Stock&#8221; above for further discussion of stock option awards and &#8220;The Spin-Off&#8201;&#8212;&#8201;Treatment of Equity Awards&#8221; above for discussion of the treatment of FedEx stock options held by FedEx Freight employees in connection with the Spin-Off. </font>
        </div>
        <div style="clear:both; padding:0pt; margin:0pt;font-size:0pt;line-height:0pt;">&#8203;</div>
        <div style=" float:left; line-height:12pt; margin-top:5.89pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:left; width:20pt;white-space:nowrap;">
          <font style=" position:relative; bottom:4.25pt;font-size:7.5pt;letter-spacing:0.15pt;">(5)</font>
          <br >
        </div>
        <div style=" margin-top:5.89pt; margin-bottom:0pt; line-height:12pt; text-align:left; margin-left:20pt;">
          <!--blacklining:none;-->
          <font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">In June&#160;2024, the FedEx Board, upon the recommendation of the FedEx CHRC, established this annual performance cash compensation plan, which provided a cash payment opportunity at the conclusion of fiscal 2025. Payment amounts were based upon the achievement of FedEx financial-performance goals for fiscal 2025 and the achievement of individual performance objectives. See &#8220;&#8212; Compensation Elements and Fiscal 2025 Amounts&#8201;&#8212;&#8201;AIC Program&#8221; above for further discussion of this plan. </font>
        </div>
        <div style="clear:both; padding:0pt; margin:0pt;font-size:0pt;line-height:0pt;">&#8203;</div>
        <div style=" float:left; line-height:12pt; margin-top:5.89pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:left; width:20pt;white-space:nowrap;">
          <font style=" position:relative; bottom:4.25pt;font-size:7.5pt;letter-spacing:0.15pt;">(6)</font>
          <br >
        </div>
        <div style=" margin-top:5.89pt; margin-bottom:0pt; line-height:12pt; text-align:left; margin-left:20pt;">
          <!--blacklining:none;-->
          <font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">The FedEx Board, upon the recommendation of the FedEx CHRC, established this long-term performance cash compensation plan in June&#160;2024. The plan provides a long-term cash payment opportunity to officers at the conclusion of fiscal 2027 if FedEx achieves (a)&#160;an aggregate EPS goal established by the FedEx Board with respect to the three-fiscal-year period 2025 through 2027 (50% of the total payout opportunity), (b)&#160;an average ROIC growth goal over the three-fiscal-year period 2025 through 2027 (25% of the total payout opportunity), and (c)&#160;a relative TSR performance goal with respect to the three-fiscal-year period 2025 through 2027 (25% of the total payout opportunity). No amounts can be earned under the plan until 2027 because achievement of the EPS, ROIC, and relative TSR goals can only be determined following the conclusion of the three-fiscal-year period. The estimated individual future payouts under the plan are set dollar amounts ranging from threshold (minimum) amounts if the EPS, ROIC, and relative TSR goals achieved are less than target, up to maximum amounts if the plan goals are substantially exceeded. There is no assurance that these estimated future payouts will be achieved. As of the Spin-Off, FedEx Freight executive officers will cease active participation in FedEx compensation and benefit plans and will begin to participate in FedEx Freight compensation and benefit plans that will be established prior to the Spin-Off. </font>
        </div>
        <div style="clear:both; padding:0pt; margin:0pt;font-size:0pt;line-height:0pt;">&#8203;</div>
        <div style="margin-top:12pt; width:456pt; line-height:12pt;font-weight:bold;">
          <font style="letter-spacing:-0.2pt;">Outstanding Equity Awards at End of Fiscal 2025</font><font style="font-weight:normal;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </font>
        </div>
        <div style="margin-top:8pt; width:456pt; line-height:12.5pt;">
          <font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">The following table sets forth for each FedEx Freight named executive officer certain information about unexercised FedEx stock options and unvested shares of restricted FedEx stock held at the end of the fiscal year ended May&#160;31, 2025. See &#8220;The Spin-Off&#8201;&#8212;&#8201;Treatment of Equity Awards&#8221; above for discussion of the treatment of FedEx equity awards held by FedEx Freight employees in connection with the Spin-Off. </font>

          <font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">If the shares were sold immediately upon exercise, the value realized on exercise of the option is the difference between the actual sales price and the exercise price of the option.         <div style=" float:left; margin-top:8.9pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:left; width:20pt;white-space:nowrap;">
          <font style=" position:relative; bottom:4.25pt;font-size:7.5pt;letter-spacing:0.15pt;">(1)</font>
          <br >
        </div>
        <div style=" margin-top:7.9pt; margin-bottom:0pt; line-height:12pt; text-align:left; margin-left:20pt;">
          <!--blacklining:none;-->
          <font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">Effective May&#160;31, 2023, the defined benefit pension plans sponsored by FedEx Freight were merged into the FedEx-sponsored defined benefit pension plans. </font>
        </div>
        <div style="clear:both; padding:0pt; margin:0pt;font-size:0pt;line-height:0pt;">&#8203;</div>
        <div style=" float:left; line-height:12pt; margin-top:3.9pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:left; width:20pt;white-space:nowrap;">
          <font style=" position:relative; bottom:4.25pt;font-size:7.5pt;letter-spacing:0.15pt;">(2)</font>
          <br >
        </div>
        <div style=" margin-top:3.9pt; margin-bottom:0pt; line-height:12pt; text-align:left; margin-left:20pt;">
          <!--blacklining:none;-->
          <font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">These amounts were determined using assumptions (e.g., for interest rates and mortality rates) consistent with those used in the audited consolidated financial statements included herein and in FedEx&#8217;s Annual Report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended May&#160;31, 2025. The benefits are expressed as lump sum amounts, even though the benefits using the traditional pension benefit formula under </font>
        </div>
        <div style="clear:both; padding:0pt; margin:0pt;font-size:0pt;line-height:0pt;">&#8203;</div>
      </div>
      <div style="margin-top:2.00000000000002pt;height:12pt;margin-left:69.66pt;width:456pt;">
        <div style="margin-top:5pt; text-align:center; width:456pt; line-height:12pt;">
          <font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">&#160;</font>
          <br >
        </div>
      </div>
      <div style="margin-top:2pt;margin-bottom:21.86pt;margin-left:69.66pt;width:456pt;">
        <div style="margin-top:5pt; text-align:center; width:456pt; line-height:12pt;">
          <font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">136</font>
          <br >
        </div>

    <div style="page-break-after:always; width:595.3pt;margin-left:auto;margin-right:auto;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;font-variant:normal;text-transform:none;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;font-size:10pt;">
      <div style="padding:0pt;margin:0pt;font-family:calibri, arial, sans-serif;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;font-size:8pt;line-height:8pt;">
        <a style="text-decoration:none;color:#003366;" href="#TOC">TABLE OF CONTENTS</a>
      </div>
      <div style="margin-top:15.85pt;height:24pt;margin-left:69.66pt;width:456pt;">
        <div style="margin-top:17pt; width:456pt; line-height:12pt;">
          <font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">&#160;</font>
          <br >
        </div>
      </div>
      <div style="margin-top:6pt;margin-left:69.66pt;width:456pt;">
        <div style="margin-left:20pt; width:436pt; line-height:12.5pt;">
          <font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">the Pension Plan (as defined below) are generally not payable as a lump sum distribution (only $5,000 or less may be distributed as a lump sum under the traditional pension benefit formula under the Pension Plan). The benefits using the Portable Pension Account formula (discussed below) under the Pension Plan may be paid as a lump sum. </font>
        </div>
        <div style="margin-left:20pt; margin-top:8pt; width:436pt; line-height:12.5pt;">
          <font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">The present value of the Pension Plan traditional pension benefit is equal to the single life annuity payable at the normal retirement date (age 60), or June&#160;1, 2025 if the officer is past normal retirement age, converted based on an interest rate of 5.942% and Oliver Wyman&#8217;s 2024 mortality tables based on the U.S. longevity model with MP-2021 mortality improvement scale, discounted to May&#160;31, 2025 using an interest rate of 5.942%. The present value of the Parity Plan (as defined below) traditional pension benefit is equal to the single life annuity payable at the normal retirement age (age 60), or June&#160;1, 2025 if the officer is past normal retirement age, converted based on an interest rate of 4.71% for lump sums paid through May&#160;31, 2026, 4.26% for lump sums paid through May&#160;31, 2027, and 3.80% for lump sums paid on and after June&#160;1, 2027, and the 1994 Group Annuity Reserving Table, discounted to May&#160;31, 2025 using an interest rate of 5.942%. The present value of the Portable Pension Account as of May&#160;31, 2025 is equal to the officer&#8217;s account balance on May&#160;31, 2025, projected to the normal retirement date, if applicable, based on an interest rate of 1.2375% credited quarterly during fiscal year 2026 and 1% credited quarterly thereafter and discounted to May&#160;31, 2025, using an interest rate of 5.942%. </font>
        </div>
        <div style="margin-left:20pt; margin-top:12pt; width:436pt; line-height:12pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">
          <font style="letter-spacing:-0.2pt;">Overview of Pension Plans</font><font style="font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </font>
        </div>
        <div style="margin-top:8pt; width:456pt; line-height:12.5pt;">
          <font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">The FedEx Freight named executive officers participate in the FedEx Corporation Retirement Savings Plan (the &#8220;401(k) Plan&#8221;). The annual matching company contribution under the 401(k) Plan is a maximum of 3.5% of eligible earnings. Effective January&#160;1, 2022, employees hired on or after January&#160;1, 2020 (or eligible employees who chose to cease receiving compensation credits under the Pension Plan (as defined below)) instead receive enhanced matching contributions up to a maximum of 8.0% of eligible earnings under the FedEx Corporation Retirement Savings Plan&#160;II (the &#8220;401(k) Plan&#160;II&#8221;). </font>
        </div>
        <div style="margin-top:8pt; width:456pt; line-height:12.5pt;">
          <font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">FedEx maintains a tax-qualified, defined benefit pension plan called the FedEx Corporation Employees&#8217; Pension Plan (the &#8220;Pension Plan&#8221;). FedEx also maintains a supplemental, non-tax-qualified plan called the FedEx Corporation Retirement Parity Pension Plan (the &#8220;Parity Plan&#8221;), which provides 100% of the benefits that would otherwise be denied to certain management-level participants in the Pension Plan due to the Code limits on accrued annual benefits and annual compensation that may be taken into account under a tax-qualified pension plan. For management-level participants who accrue Pension Plan benefits under a formula applicable to FedEx Freight employees (including Messrs. McCoy and Lyons), the Parity Plan also provides the additional benefits those employees would have received had they accrued Pension Plan benefits under formulas applicable to employees of certain other FedEx companies. Benefits under the Parity Plan are unfunded and are general, unsecured obligations of FedEx. </font>
        </div>
        <div style="margin-top:8pt; width:456pt; line-height:12.5pt;">
          <font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">Effective May&#160;31, 2003, FedEx amended the Pension Plan and the Parity Plan to add a cash balance feature, which is called the Portable Pension Account. Eligible employees hired after May&#160;31, 2003 accrue benefits exclusively under the Portable Pension Account and benefits previously accrued using the traditional pension benefit formula were capped as of May&#160;31, 2008, and are payable beginning at retirement. Parity Plan participants, including the FedEx Freight named executive officers, receive additional Portable Pension Account compensation credits equal to 3.5% of any eligible earnings above the maximum compensation limit for tax-qualified plans (or 8% after January&#160;1, 2022 for eligible employees who elect to receive enhanced matching contributions under the 401(k) Plan&#160;II, as described above, or who were hired on or after January&#160;1, 2020). </font>
        </div>
        <div style="margin-top:8pt; width:456pt; line-height:12.5pt;">
          <font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">Normal retirement age for the majority of participants under the Pension Plan and the Parity Plan is age&#160;60, except that for benefits accrued after January&#160;31, 2016, the normal retirement age is age 62 and for benefits accrued at FedEx Freight the normal retirement age is 65. The traditional pension benefit under the Pension Plan for a participant who retires between the ages of 55 and 60 will be reduced by 3% for each year the participant receives his or her benefit prior to age 60. </font>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div style="margin-top:2.00000000000002pt;height:12pt;margin-left:69.66pt;width:456pt;">
        <div style="margin-top:5pt; text-align:center; width:456pt; line-height:12pt;">

      <div style="margin-top:6pt;margin-left:69.66pt;width:456pt;">
        <div style="margin-left:20pt; width:436pt; line-height:12pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">
          <font style="letter-spacing:-0.2pt;">Traditional Pension Benefit</font><font style="font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </font>
        </div>
        <div style="margin-top:8pt; width:456pt; line-height:12pt;">
          <font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">Under the traditional pension benefit formula, the Pension Plan and the Parity Plan provide an accrued benefit equal to 2% of the average of the five calendar&#160;years (three calendar&#160;years for the Parity Plan) of highest earnings during employment multiplied by&#160;years of credited service for benefit accrual up to 25&#160;years. Eligible compensation for the traditional pension benefit under the Pension Plan and the Parity Plan generally include salary and annual incentive compensation. </font>
        </div>
        <div style="margin-top:8pt; width:456pt; line-height:12pt;">
          <font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">Each FedEx Freight named executive officer&#8217;s capped accrued traditional pension benefit was calculated using his&#160;years of credited service as of either May&#160;31, 2003 or May&#160;31, 2008, depending on whether he chose to accrue future benefits under the cash balance formula or the traditional pension benefit formula in 2003, and his eligible earnings history as of May&#160;31, 2008. </font>
        </div>
        <div style="margin-left:20pt; margin-top:12pt; width:436pt; line-height:12pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">
          <font style="letter-spacing:-0.2pt;">Portable Pension Account</font><font style="font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </font>
        </div>
        <div style="margin-top:8pt; width:456pt; line-height:12pt;">
          <font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">The benefit under the Portable Pension Account is expressed as a notional cash balance account. For each plan year in which a participant is credited with a year of service, compensation credits, equal to a stated&#160;percentage of annual compensation, are added based on the FedEx company by which the participant is employed and the participant&#8217;s age and&#160;years of service as of the end of the prior plan year and the participant&#8217;s eligible compensation for the prior calendar year, in accordance with the following table: </font>

          <font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">On May&#160;31, 2025, the sum of age plus&#160;years of service for the FedEx Freight named executive officers was as follows: Mr.&#160;Smith&#8201;&#8212;&#8201;86; Mr.&#160;Klank&#8201;&#8212;&#8201;82; Mr.&#160;McCoy&#8201;&#8212;&#8201;77; and Mr.&#160;Lyons&#8201;&#8212;&#8201;61. The difference between the Portable Pension Account benefits which Mr.&#160;McCoy and Mr.&#160;Lyons accrued and the benefits they would have accrued under the compensation crediting rate for Federal Express and FedEx is addressed by the Parity Plan. Eligible compensation under the Portable Pension Account and Parity Plan features include salary, annual incentive compensation, and promotional and certain other bonuses (but does not include long-term incentive compensation). </font>

      <div style="margin-top:6pt;margin-left:69.66pt;width:456pt;">
        <div style="width:456pt; line-height:11.5pt;">
          <font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">An eligible participant will receive transition compensation credits for five&#160;years (through May&#160;31, 2013) or until he or she has 25&#160;years of credited service, whichever is longer. For participants with 25 or more&#160;years of service, transition compensation credits are 2% per year and ceased as of May&#160;31, 2013. An eligible participant&#8217;s first transition compensation credit was added to his or her Portable Pension Account as of May&#160;31, 2009. </font>
        </div>
        <div style="margin-top:8pt; width:456pt; line-height:11.5pt;">
          <font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">Interest credits are added to a participant&#8217;s Portable Pension Account benefit as of the end of each fiscal quarter (August&#160;31, November&#160;30, February&#160;28, and May&#160;31) after a participant accrues his or her first compensation credit, except that the May&#160;31 interest credit is added prior to the May&#160;31 compensation credit or transition compensation credit (or additional compensation credit under the Parity Plan). Interest credits are based on the Portable Pension Account notional balance and a quarterly interest-crediting factor, which is equal to the greater of (a)&#160;1/4 of the one-year Treasury constant maturities rate for April of the preceding plan year plus 0.25% and (b)&#160;1% (1/4 of 4%). Interest credits will continue to be added until the last day of the month before plan benefits are distributed. The quarterly interest-crediting factor for the plan year ended May&#160;31, 2025 was 1.535%, the plan year ended May&#160;31, 2024 was 1.420%, and the plan year ended May&#160;31, 2023 was 1.000%. </font>
        </div>
        <div style="margin-left:20pt; margin-top:12pt; width:436pt; line-height:12pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">
          <font style="letter-spacing:-0.2pt;">Distribution</font><font style="font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </font>
        </div>
        <div style="margin-top:8pt; width:456pt; line-height:11.5pt;">
          <font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">Upon a participant&#8217;s retirement, the vested traditional pension benefit under the Pension Plan is payable as a monthly annuity. Upon a participant&#8217;s retirement or other termination of employment, an amount equal to the vested Portable Pension Account notional balance under the Pension Plan is payable to the participant in the form of a lump-sum payment or an annuity. </font>
        </div>
        <div style="margin-top:8pt; width:456pt; line-height:12pt;">
          <font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">All Parity Plan benefits are paid as a single lump-sum distribution as follows: </font>
        </div>
        <div style=" float:left; margin-left:20pt; line-height:12pt; margin-top:5.8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:left; width:10pt;white-space:nowrap;">
          <font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">&#8226;</font>
          <br >
        </div>
        <div style=" margin-top:5.8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; line-height:12pt; text-align:left; margin-left:30pt;">
          <!--blacklining:none;-->
          <font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">For the portion of the benefit accrued under the Portable Pension Account formula, the lump-sum benefit will be paid six&#160;months following the date of the participant&#8217;s termination of employment; and </font>
        </div>
        <div style="clear:both; padding:0pt; margin:0pt;font-size:0pt;line-height:0pt;">&#8203;</div>
        <div style=" float:left; margin-left:20pt; line-height:12pt; margin-top:5.81pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:left; width:10pt;white-space:nowrap;">
          <font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;">&#8226;</font>
          <br >
        </div>
